title: Creation, every moment (ST I.104)
hookLine: God doesn't just start the world; he holds it in being now

lines: A ROOM LIT ONLY WHILE LIGHT SHINES.
cards: A lamp is on in a room at night. Switch it off and the room goes dark at once; the light doesn't linger out of habit. A room is lit only while something shines into it.

It's easy to hear creation as an event far back: a first morning, God starting things up and then, maybe, stepping back to watch them run. Thomas Aquinas thought that picture leaves out what matters most.
Today's word is creation, in the present tense.

teach.h: THE SUN AND THE BRIGHT AIR.
teach.b: In the Summa, Thomas asks whether creatures need God to keep them in being. His answer: yes, every creature, every moment. His image is the sun and the air.
The air is bright while the sun shines on it; the brightness isn't something the air owns. Take the sun away and the air is dark. So it is, he says, between God and everything that exists.
A house keeps standing after the builder goes home, because the builder only arranged bricks that were already there. God doesn't arrange what was already there.
He gives things their being, and no creature can hold that up by itself. Thomas cites Augustine: if the Creator's power ever stopped, all things would stop with it.
Remember from the first way: reason alone, Thomas says, can't prove the world had a beginning in time. He holds that it did, by faith.
So creation, for him, is first of all not a date. It's dependence: being held. And keeping things in being isn't a second act God adds later.
It's the same act that gives being, simply continuing. Hebrews, in the Douay-Rheims, speaks of Christ "upholding all things by the word of his power."

teach.h: FOR IN HIM WE LIVE, AND MOVE, AND ARE.
teach.b: And Paul tells the Athenians: "For in him we live, and move, and are." Put this beside yesterday. If God is being itself, everything else has its being from him, not once, but now.
The chair under you. Your hands. The person who annoyed you this morning.
Not wound up and left running. Held.

how: Catholics profess God as creator of heaven and earth in the Creed at Mass, and teachers in the tradition of Thomas often explain creation as God's ongoing gift of being, not only a first event.

o: God giving everything its being, right now
the one first morning when the world began
God shaping matter that already existed

games.q: creation, every moment — tap the pairs.
p: keeps the air bright while it shines
goes home; the house still stands
being held, not only a beginning
in him we live, and move, and are

s: for Thomas, creation only means the world's first moment
for Thomas, creation is first of all dependence: God gives things their being now, not only once.
for Thomas, keeping things in being is the same act that gives them being, continuing
it isn't a second act God adds later; the gift of being simply goes on.
in Thomas's picture, God is like a builder who can go home
the house outlasts the builder. creatures don't outlast God's gift of being: take the sun away and the air goes dark.

games.q: you're Thomas. a student says: God made the world long ago, and now it runs on its own, like a house after the builder leaves. what do you answer?
o: say the world needs God to keep it in being, as the air needs the sun to stay bright.
say the world was never created at all.
games.why: Thomas answers that every creature depends on God for its being at every moment. the builder picture fits arranging bricks, not giving being.

practice: Feel the weight of your body on the chair or the floor: something is holding you up, and it isn't you. Go one layer deeper, to your being here at all, breath arriving unasked, a heart keeping its own time.
If you pray, say the line from Acts slowly, in him we live, and move, and are; if you don't, simply rest in the fact that this moment was handed to you.

wordCard.voice: Creation. For Thomas, not only a beginning long ago, but God giving everything its being, right now, the way the sun keeps the air bright. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin, the language Thomas wrote in: creation, the making of something's being.

carryVoice: Your line: held now. The cup in your hand, another hand: each one held in being this very moment. That's the week.
